issues.legal_issue: A pleading amendment sought after commencement of trial may be refused when the applicant fails to show due diligence and the amendment is belated, changes the suit’s character, withdraws an admission, and seriously prejudices the opposing party.
material_facts: The suit sought partition and separate possession, and the original pleading proceeded on the basis that the family properties remained joint.
After evidence had been recorded and the suit was listed for final arguments, several plaintiffs sought to amend the plaint to assert that the properties had already been partitioned.
The applicants knew of the asserted earlier partition when a compromise petition referring to it was filed in the suit, but gave no explanation for waiting years to seek amendment.
The opposing plaintiff disputed that any partition had occurred and sought to continue the partition proceedings.
The proposed amendment would replace the original position that partition had not taken place, change the nature of the suit, and seriously prejudice the opposing plaintiff.
issues.conclusion: The application to amend the plaint was properly rejected; the order setting aside the trial court’s permission to amend was confirmed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, after trial has commenced an amendment may be allowed only if the applicant satisfies the court that, despite due diligence, the matter could not have been raised earlier. The applicant bears that burden, and amendment is not a matter of right. An amendment may be refused if it introduces a wholly different or inconsistent case, changes the fundamental character of the suit, is not bona fide, or causes prejudice to the other side that cannot be adequately compensated. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: civil_suit_pleading_amendment and trial_commenced and due_diligence_not_shown and (unexplained_delay or prior_knowledge_not_acted_on) and (changes_suit_character or withdraws_pleading_admission) and causes_serious_prejudice_to_opponent

predicates.civil_suit_pleading_amendment: A party sought to amend a pleading in a civil suit.
predicates.trial_commenced: The application was made after the trial had begun.
predicates.due_diligence_not_shown: The applicant did not establish that, despite acting with due diligence, the matter could not have been raised earlier.
predicates.unexplained_delay: The applicant waited a substantial time to seek amendment without explaining the delay.
predicates.prior_knowledge_not_acted_on: The applicant knew of the matter later proposed for pleading but did not seek amendment within a reasonable time.
predicates.changes_suit_character: The proposed amendment would fundamentally alter the nature or character of the suit.
predicates.withdraws_pleading_admission: The proposed amendment would retract an admission in the existing pleading.
predicates.causes_serious_prejudice_to_opponent: Allowing the amendment would cause serious prejudice to the opposing party.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to amend a civil pleading after trial has begun, has not shown due diligence, and the delayed amendment would change the suit’s character or withdraw an admission while seriously prejudicing the opponent, the amendment is refused.
